pages.text: "My swing!" Lulu hopped on the wooden plank swing in the olive tree. Summer sunshine dappled through the leaves. Lulu pushed with both feet.
Three cousins waited in a row beneath the tree. "One turn, Lulu!" "A little longer!" Lulu stayed on.
Still Lulu did not get off. The cousins sat down and traced dirt with their toes. Only the swing creaked beneath the tree.
Mom watched beside the swing. "How would you feel if you were waiting there?" Lulu thought. "I would be upset too."
"Shall we count how long you swing?" Mom touched Lulu's bell. Back and forth—jingle, jingle! "Ten jingles means next turn."
Lulu stopped and put both feet down. "Everyone! One, line up!" Four lined up beneath the tree, Lulu first.
"Two, count ten jingles!" Jingle, jingle... The tenth! Lulu hopped off. "Ten jingles, next turn!"
"Three, finished counting? Next friend!" The youngest cousin climbed on. At the line's back, Lulu stamped both feet but did not step out.
Next day, four gathered at the yard tub too. Lulu raised a forepaw. "Take turns! One, line up! Two, count ten jingles! Three, finished counting? Next friend!"
Mom stood behind the swing, cradling Lulu's back and pushing gently. Wait a little, and everyone gets a turn. Ten jingles, next turn! "I will count this time!" the youngest cousin called.
